question:
A 56-year-old female daycare worker presents with a 10-day history of symptoms including watery
diarrhea, cramping in the abdomen, bloating, loss of appetite, and a weight loss of 2.3 kg. Examination
of a stool sample reveals the presence of motile trophozoites. Which of the following therapeutic agents
would be the most appropriate treatment choice? Answer Choices: (A) Iodoquinol (B) Ornidazole (C)
Furazolidone (D) Tinidazole (E) Metronidazole (F) Albendazole (G) Diloxanide furoate (H) Secnidazole
(I) Nitazoxanide (J) Paromomycin

A. Diloxanide furoate
B. Ornidazole
C. Tinidazole
D. Albendazole
E. Metronidazole
F. Furazolidone
G. Paromomycin
H. Secnidazole
I. Iodoquinol
J. Nitazoxanide
